meta.title: The Writer from the Old Town

paragraphs: The Writer from the Old Town, posted by Lily. On Thursday, Guide Ann visited the Explorers in the school library. She told us about a woman from our old town. Her name was Nora Webb, and she lived many years ago. The Explorers sat in a circle, and nobody moved. She was a worker, then a secretary, and then a writer. Guide Ann said, "Her life is a good story."

Nora was born in a small house near the river. Her family was poor, and her mother was a worker at the market. She had two brothers, and the three children shared one small room. The river was loud in the rainy season, and she liked the sound. As a child, she loved stories. Every Saturday, she walked to the town library and borrowed one book. She read it at night with a small lamp.

At the age of fifteen, she left school and began her first job. She worked in a small factory, and she cut paper all day. At the age of eighteen, she became a secretary in an office near the market. A secretary writes letters and answers the telephone, and she was very good at it. She was always on time, and she never forgot a letter. Her boss was kind, and he gave her a new book every month. "You write very well," he said.

After work, she wrote stories about the old town. She wrote at the kitchen table until midnight. Sometimes she was tired, but she wrote one page every night. She earned only a little money, so she kept her job at the office. At the age of thirty, she finished her first book. It was about the old town path, the market, and the people.

The book was a great success. Many people in the town bought it. With the money, she left the office and chose a new occupation, writer. Her career was long, and she wrote nine books. The town library has all of them. A teacher at the school read the first book aloud to a class.

Guide Ann uses the first book when she takes visitors on a walk. "The writer was our best guide," she said. We borrowed the book, and Mia took a photo of the cover. Maybe one day, one of us will write a book about our town. Who will it be?
